Alright, the recent actions have set up a custom development server (`devserver.py`) that can accept a POST to `/snap` and write the incoming base64 JPEG to a file. I edited `.claude/launch.json` so that the launch configuration now runs `devserver.py` instead of the default `http.server` module. After updating the launch config, I attempted to start the preview server with `mcp__Claude_Preview__preview_start name="wildwood"`. The system reported that a server with the same name was already running (the original http.server instance) and simply reused it, meaning my new `devserver.py` code never actually got executed. To get the new server code to run, I need to stop the existing server and start a fresh one.

I called `ToolSearch` for a stop command, found none, then explicitly invoked `mcp__Claude_Preview__preview_stop` with the old `serverId`. That succeeded, terminating the previous http.server process. Immediately after, I called `preview_start` again with the same name. This time the system created a brand‑new server instance (new `serverId` 8bd6aa05-4e60-4172-ae78-3b1806af072b) and reported that it was not reused, confirming that the new `devserver.py` is now the active handler.

Now that the new server is up, the page that the preview is showing in the browser is still loaded from the old server context. To make the browser connect to the freshly started server (which now includes the `/snap` POST endpoint), I need to reload the page in that preview environment. The only way to trigger a reload from this side is to evaluate JavaScript in the preview context. The appropriate expression is `location.reload(); 'reloading'`, which will cause the page to refresh and then return the string `'reloading'` so I get a simple confirmation result.

Therefore, the next logical step is to issue a `preview_eval` call on the new server ID with that reload expression. This will ensure the client reloads, picks up the new server code, and I can then test the screenshot POST endpoint again.
